rationale: The ticket fixes the refresh-to-storage path so a re-check keeps the sale details the item-page parser already observes; scope is refresh-to-storage only, so the four criteria are pinned by four behaviour-named fixtures that drive the real ListingRefreshService and real ScrapeStore over an isolated temp SQLite database with the existing StubScrapeClient, then read the persisted ListingEntity and ListingStatusChanges back. No production shape is declared because every assertion is expressed through public surfaces that already exist (ListingRefreshService, ScrapeStore, EtlDbContext, ListingEntity, StubScrapeClient); the tests fail at base purely because ScrapeStore.RecordStatusChange drops the sale details, so no signature has to change for the contract to compile. Measured at base: Should_store_the_observed_sold_price_and_sold_date_after_a_sold_recheck is red (SoldPrice null, SoldDate null) and Should_set_the_stored_sold_flag_after_a_sold_recheck is red (IsSold false); the ended and still-active fixtures are green regression guards that pin the must-not-break outcomes (status recorded, no invented sold price, active values untouched). Running the repository gate (.githooks/pre-commit) shows only those two contract failures among 84 Unit tests (82 pass) plus Architecture 25/25 and a clean dotnet format, so there is no collateral and declaredRedTests is empty.
